item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record is mixed but leans negative on 5B.4. He did appoint credible economic officials and accepted IMF-backed reform language aimed at business climate and job creation. But the year’s stronger evidence still points to weak enforcement, opaque procurement, mining-linked land harms, and a broader investment environment that remained far from fair or predictable.

**Accepted Claims**
- [DR Congo president appoints country’s first female prime minister](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | Tshisekedi elevated Judith Suminwa, then planning minister, into the top executive role. That is a real pro-competence signal for economic governance, though it is appointment evidence rather than proof of fair market rules. `5B.4` `5B.2` `E0334`

- [Biographie de la Première Ministre](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/biographie-de-la-premiere-ministre/) | Primature | 2024 | Suminwa’s biography emphasizes applied economics, banking experience, UN/PNUD work, budget-ministry experience, and leadership on the 145 Territories program and the 2024-2028 development plan. This supports the view that Tshisekedi chose a capable economic professional rather than a pure loyalist. `5B.4` `5B.2` `E0335`

- [ProfilMin.php](https://adminfinances.cd/ProfilMin.php) | Administration des Finances | 2024 | Doudou Fwamba’s profile shows economics and public-finance credentials plus long experience inside the finance administration. That is strong evidence for a merit-based economic appointment. `5B.4` `5B.2` `E0336`

- [IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo on an Extended Credit Facility and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | IMF | 2024-11-13 | The IMF program was framed around inclusive growth, diversification, job creation, governance, transparency, and business-environment improvement. It also called for tighter expenditure-chain controls, Treasury reforms, lower tax exemptions, better customs enforcement, and more protection from extractive-revenue volatility. `5B.4` `5B.3` `E0338`

- [Deux nouveaux programmes avec le FMI: Aimé Boji et Doudou Fwamba étaient devant la presse](https://budget.gouv.cd/deux-nouveaux-programmes-avec-le-fmi-aime-boji-et-doudou-fwamba-etaient-devant-la-presse/) | Ministère du Budget | 2024-11-15 | The budget ministry said the finance and budget ministers jointly presented the IMF programs and credited improved coordination since June 2024. This suggests the economic team was actually being used to execute policy, not just serve as window dressing. `5B.4` `5B.3` `5B.2` `E0341`

- [Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is direct evidence against fair, competitive, and transparent public administration. `5B.4` `E0329`

- [DRC president Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, social services were underfunded, and mining expansion was driving forced evictions and pollution. This is strong negative evidence for property-rights security and long-term investment conditions, especially in extractives. `5B.4` `E0330`

- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Congo, Democratic Republic of: April 2024 - Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099434404082425237) | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | The World Bank said growth prospects were favorable, but living standards would not improve without much more ambitious reforms and that deficits, inflation, and downside risks remained. This is indirect but important counterevidence: the rule environment was still not producing broad, reliable market confidence. `5B.4` `E0328`

**Search Gap**
I did not find a 2024 source showing a comprehensive legal overhaul of land titles, competition policy, bankruptcy, customs, or court enforcement under Tshisekedi. The strongest pro evidence is mostly about appointments and IMF reform design; the strongest negative evidence is about corruption, opaque procurement, and mining-related property harms, not a clean before/after reform success.
